wiring.title: What a start runs on
wiring.body: For each workspace: the agent, account and version a driven session would start with — and an intake, once an agent is named for it — and which setting chose each. The driver reads this same answer.
chain.title: How this work ran
chain.unseen: an earlier step this page does not hold
chain.pendingHint: Each step is published when the one before it closes done, on behalf of the same asker; a decline stops the chain.
projects.fedTip: this deployment's copy came from commit {{commit}} on {{branch}}, fed by {{origin}}. Only the canonical line feeds knowledge, and a newer commit replaces an older one.
settings.title: Settings
settings.workspaces.title: {{count}} workspace
settings.workspaces.none: A workspace exists once a repository is registered in it. Projects says how one joins.
settings.description: How this window looks and speaks, then what is true about this machine.
settings.descriptionBrowser: How this window looks and speaks. A machine's own settings are on the desktop, where the machine is.
settings.theme.label: Theme
settings.theme.hint: System follows the computer's own light or dark setting.
settings.language.label: Language
settings.language.hint: The window's own words; what the service says is shown as it said it.
settings.ai.body: The jobs Daoris may use a model for. Each does its part with none, and says which tier answered.
settings.ai.search.label: Search and convergence
settings.ai.search.hint: The service reads `DAORIS_EMBED_MODEL` (a model's name) and `DAORIS_EMBED_URL` (its endpoint; Ollama's local address unless set) from its environment when it starts, so a change takes a restart of the service.
settings.ai.search.why: With no model, search matches words and convergence finds copies and restatements; both still answer, and say which tier did. A model adds what comparing text cannot: two repositories that reached the same conclusion in different words. Which model is the deployment's choice, never the feature's.
settings.ai.intake.label: Intake
settings.ai.intake.hint: Also `daoris driver intake <agent>|off` — the same driver.json field, read every tick.
settings.ai.intake.why: An ask names no repository. The workspace's declarations answer it first, with no model, and what they leave is proposed to you. With an agent named here, those asks open a session on it instead: it reads the declarations, publishes the quests, and asks you where it cannot tell. Every intake spends a real login.
settings.ai.intake.tierOff: Asks are answered from the workspace's declarations; what they leave is proposed to you.
settings.ai.intake.tierOn: Declarations first; an ask they leave opens a session on {{agent}} — a login each.
settings.ai.intake.named: An ask the declarations leave now opens an intake session on {{agent}}.
settings.ai.intake.cleared: Asks on this machine are answered by declarations only now.
settings.rules.hint: Claude Code's own permission rules, handed to every session Daoris starts. Also `daoris agent rules`: the same file.
settings.rules.why: Anything a session Daoris starts would have to ask for is refused: nobody is there to answer. So what it needs is allowed before it starts, and what it must never do is denied. These rules are one more scope beside yours and the repository's, and the agent's own order decides: deny beats ask beats allow. So a repository's deny still wins over anything allowed here. Sessions on other agents are handed none of these.
settings.rules.addBody: A tool name, with a specifier in parentheses when it needs one: Bash(npm run test:*), Edit(/docs/**), WebFetch(domain:example.com). Sessions started from now on are handed it. An ask is a refusal here, because nobody is there to answer it.
settings.rules.removed: {{rule}} is no longer a rule for {{where}}.
settings.rules.switched: The default {{id}} is {{state}} on this machine.
settings.rules.proposals.title: Proposed by agents
settings.rules.proposals.hint: A session may propose a change to these rules. One that narrows what agents may do applied itself at the driver's next tick; one that widens it waits here for your yes. Also `daoris agent rules proposals`.
settings.rules.proposals.byUnknown: a session the driver did not start
settings.rules.proposals.widens: It widens what agents may do, so it waits for your yes.
settings.rules.proposals.unjudged: The driver has not judged it yet. If it narrows what agents may do, it applies itself at the next tick.
settings.rules.proposals.accepted: Accepted: {{change}}. Sessions started from now on are handed it.
settings.rules.proposals.declined: Declined: {{change}}. The rules are as they were.
settings.home.label: Daoris home
settings.home.hint: The Daoris home. Every file on this page lives under it, and a terminal's daoris reads the same folder; nothing of Daoris's lives under your profile.
settings.wiring.title: Wiring
settings.wiring.label: Remotes map
settings.wiring.hint: Which deployment serves each workspace here. A workspace with no entry stays local — the default, and no setting.
settings.wiring.body: What a repository may send is its own manifest's call; this only says where it would go. A shared deployment serves one workspace and refuses a registration declaring another.
settings.wiring.none: Nothing is wired — every workspace on this machine stays local.
settings.wiring.fromEnvironment: The environment names this machine's remote, whole — the file below is not read while DAORIS_REMOTE_URL and DAORIS_REMOTE_KEY are set. What is listed is what is in effect.
settings.wiring.keyBody: The key is minted on the deployment's own console, per person per machine. It is stored in the file and never tracked, shown back, or sent anywhere but that deployment.
settings.wiring.keyTip: the key's audit prefix — the same handle the deployment's own key list shows
settings.wiring.unwired: {{workspace}} syncs nowhere from here now. Nothing at the deployment changed.
settings.wiring.wiredButOverridden: {{workspace}} is written to the map — but the environment names this machine's remote, so the file is not what is in effect. Unset it to use what you just wired.
errors.REMOTE_HALF_DECLARED: {{workspace}} needs both an address and a key. A half-declared remote is no remote — one written into the map would simply be skipped.
errors.REPOSITORY_NOT_ADOPTED: {{repository}} has not adopted Daoris, so there is no declaration to edit. Its own agent runs the adoption; this form changes one that already exists.
errors.DRIVER_NOT_READY: The driver is still coming up — its service is not answering yet. A moment.
errors.SERVICE_UNREACHABLE: The service is not answering. What is on screen is the last it said, until it answers again.
errors.HARNESS_ACTION_UNKNOWN: There is no agent action called {{action}}.
errors.HARNESS_ACTION_IDLE: Nothing is running for {{harness}} {{action}} — it finished, or was never started.
errors.HARNESS_ACTION_BUSY: {{running}} is still running — wait for it to end, or stop it, before starting another.
errors.PLUGIN_UNKNOWN: There is no plugin called {{id}} on this machine.
errors.PLUGIN_ACTION_UNKNOWN: There is no plugin action called {{action}}.
errors.PLUGIN_BUSY: {{id}} was not removed: something on this machine still has a file in its folder open. Close it and remove it again — nothing was taken.
errors.SESSION_MOVE_NOT_YOURS: A person may finish, decline or stop a parked session — not move it to {{state}}. Answering it so it carries on is a message, not a move.
errors.SESSION_DECLINE_NEEDS_REASON: Declining needs a reason: it is the part whoever reads this record can act on.
errors.SESSION_NOT_REVIEWABLE: This session's work is not on this machine — its record names no working tree here, as a record that came from another machine never does.
errors.SESSION_NO_BASE: This session's record does not say which commit it started from, so there is no range to measure — a record from before Daoris wrote that down keeps its evidence line only.
errors.SESSION_RANGE_UNREADABLE: git could not read this session's range where it ran — its tree has moved, been discarded, or no longer holds the commit it started from.
errors.SESSION_TREE_UNLISTED: git cannot list this session's files here — its tree is not on this machine, is gone, or is not a repository of its own. A path you type after @ still reaches the agent.
errors.WINDOW_UNKNOWN: {{name}} is not a window this build opens. There are two: the monitor, and one session on its own.
errors.UNKNOWN: Something on this machine refused, and did not say why. The driver's log has the detail.
errors.TIMEOUT: This machine did not answer in time — the driver may be busy. Try again in a moment.
errors.NO_TRANSPORT: This page is not connected to Daoris's desktop, so it cannot ask this machine anything.
errors.NO_HANDLER: This window has no part called {{module}} — the page is newer or older than the application. Restart Daoris.
errors.NO_ROUTE: {{module}} does not know {{type}} — the page is newer or older than the application. Restart Daoris.
errors.SCOPE_REQUIRED: {{module}} needs to be told which window it is for, and was not.
errors.MISSING_PAYLOAD_VALUE: The request was missing something it needs — the page is newer or older than the application.
errors.INVALID_PAYLOAD_VALUE: The request carried a value this application does not accept — the page is newer or older than the application.
errors.CAPABILITY_NOT_SUPPORTED: This window cannot do that here.
errors.UNKNOWN_ERROR: Something on this machine failed, and did not say why. The driver's log has the detail.
harness.title: Agent tools
harness.body: Which account each tool runs as
usage.title: What each account has carried
usage.body: Context reported by the sessions and conversations this machine ran, per account, each at its highest. A door that carries only text reports none, so a session run on one is an absence here, not a zero. No price is attached.
usage.contextTip: context held, summed across that account's sessions, each at its own high-water mark. The agent's own units, as it reported them.
usage.note: Measured, not billed — and never sent anywhere. These numbers stay on this machine, like the transcripts and the account names they belong to.
harness.pin.fromPathAbsent: runs from PATH once it is there
harness.pin.managedTip: the binary Daoris installed and runs sessions with. Daoris owns this location; the tool inside it is the tool's own.
plugin.body: A plugin is a folder here with a plugin.json: it declares agents sessions can run on, and may speak — a process of its own the driver asks before a start and tells of an ending. No code from a plugin ever runs inside Daoris.
plugin.none: No plugins — copy a folder in with `daoris plugin add <folder>`.
plugin.forgetTip: Deletes the install folder. What the plugin kept, beside it under .data, stays — yours to delete, never Daoris's.
plugin.enabled: {{id}} is on. The driver asks it from its next look.
plugin.disabled: {{id}} is off. It stays where it is; the driver stops asking it at its next look.
plugin.removedKept: {{id}} is removed from this machine. What it kept is still at {{data}}.
plugin.terminal: Also `daoris plugin list|add|remove|enable|disable` — the same folder and the same file, either door.
harness.profile.note: An account is made by signing in: the tool's own sign-in runs into a configuration directory Daoris owns the location of, and every way into a tool shares it. Each tool installs and updates by its own mechanism, never automatically; pin a version and sessions run on a copy Daoris installs somewhere it owns, unpinned they run whatever this machine has on PATH.
harness.profile.keyHint: Kept on this machine by Daoris, handed to the agent when a session starts, and shown back only as its last four characters.
harness.profile.removeConfirm: This deletes the account from this machine, sign-in included. Sessions that used it go back to the tool's own account.
harness.ownHome: the tool's own configuration home — sign in with the tool itself; Daoris never touches it
harness.login.hint: Log in runs the tool's own sign-in here on this row: a page opens, you paste the code it shows, and the account is ready when it reads logged in.
harness.login.done: {{profile}} is signed in — sessions can run as it.
harness.login.failed: Sign-in did not finish (the tool exited {{code}}). Its output says why.
harness.loginNew.done: Signed in as {{account}} — sessions can run as it.
harness.loginNew.unnamed: Signed in — the tool did not say who, so the account is listed as {{profile}}.
harness.loginNew.nobody: Nobody was signed in, so nothing was kept.
harness.loginNew.failed: Sign-in did not finish (the tool exited {{code}}), so nothing was kept. Its output says why.
signin.title: Signing in to {{profile}}
signin.readyNew: The account appears above, under who signed in, once the sign-in finishes. If it does not finish, nothing is kept.
signin.step.open: Sign in on the page that opened.
signin.step.openHint: No browser? Copy the link into one.
signin.waiting: Waiting for the tool to open the page…
signin.opened: The tool opened your browser — finish signing in there, and this row will say so.
signin.step.code: If the page shows you a code, paste it here.
signin.codeLater: The box appears when the tool asks for one — most sign-ins finish in the browser.
signin.sent: Code sent — the tool is finishing.
signin.ready: The account is ready when the row reads logged in.
harness.homeTip: the configuration directory Daoris owns the location of. What is inside it belongs to the tool.
harness.login.keyedTip: The tool says signed in for any key, a wrong one included. A key is checked the first time a session uses it.
harness.failed: {{harness}}: {{action}} exited {{code}}. The output above is the agent's own.
harness.secrets: A sign-in is the tool's: logging in runs its own flow inside the account's directory, and whatever it obtains the tool stores itself. An API key is the one secret Daoris keeps, and only when you give it one.
sidebar.absent: Not found where the registry says: {{names}} — registered here, and nothing of it is in this refresh.
scope.label: workspace
scope.tip: Which workspace this window is scoped to. Knowledge, quests and records cross within a workspace and never across one; with nothing chosen the console spans every workspace this deployment holds — and says so here rather than mixing them.
statusHint.Taken: a repository's agent has accepted it
statusHint.Declined: turned down — the note is the part the asker can act on
overview.title: Overview
overview.description: Is anything sitting, and is the family healthy — the state of the thing being managed.
overview.tiles.adopted.label: Adopted projects
overview.tiles.open.label: Open quests
overview.tiles.open.noteUnderDay: oldest has sat under a day
overview.tiles.progress.label: In progress
overview.tiles.knowledge.label: Knowledge entries
overview.outstanding.title: Outstanding — oldest first
overview.outstanding.sittingTip: why this machine's driver is not starting it, in its own words, as of its last look.
overview.outstanding.emptyBody: The family owes itself nothing right now. When a project needs something from a sibling, it is asked for here.
overview.repositories.title: Repositories, by what the index holds
overview.repositories.emptyBody: A registered repository's knowledge appears here after the next refresh.
overview.repositories.adoptedDot: adopted — its own declaration and doctrine
overview.repositories.hint: ● adopted — it carries its own declaration and doctrine. The others have not adopted, and one registered with a root here can still be asked a quest. “Local” is the repository's own material — the part no sibling can reach without this index.
quests.title: Quests
quests.description: What has been asked of whom — held by the service, pulled by each repository's own agent, never written into anyone's tree.
quests.empty.body: The family owes itself nothing right now. When a project needs something from a sibling, it is asked for here — never edited across.
quests.detail.retried: #{{id}} will be tried again at the driver's next look. {{count}} more failed sessions park it again.
quests.detail.declinePlaceholder: the reason — it is the part the asker can act on
quests.detail.fileElsewhere: kept on the machine that published it
quests.detail.conflictsHint: Another machine's move reached the remote first. What this one attempted is kept here for a person; nothing was merged.
asks.tier.declarations: by declarations only; no intake harness ran
asks.compose.title: Ask the workspace
asks.compose.meta: kept by the service until it becomes quests
asks.compose.nowhere.headline: There is no workspace to ask yet
asks.compose.nowhere.body: An ask is made in a workspace, and a workspace exists once a repository is registered in it. Projects says how one joins.
asks.compose.hint: Say what is wanted and why, with the ticket's links and files. The workspace's declarations propose where it belongs, and nothing is published until you name a receiver or accept a proposal.
asks.compose.hintIntake: Say what is wanted and why, with the ticket's links and files. This machine's intake agent reads it and publishes it where it belongs, and asks you when it cannot tell. Naming a receiver publishes it at once.
asks.compose.hintUnknown: Say what is wanted and why, with the ticket's links and files. Naming a receiver publishes it at once. Otherwise the workspace's declarations propose where it belongs, or the machine's intake agent, where one is set, reads it and publishes.
asks.compose.toNobody: nobody yet — let the declarations propose
asks.compose.filesLabel: files — kept on this machine until the ask becomes quests, then carried by each
asks.record.noProposal: No repository's declarations share its words. Name the receiver below.
asks.record.anotherPlaceholder: any repository in workspace {{circle}} that can be asked
asks.record.fileKept: kept on this machine until it becomes quests
asks.tier.intake: an intake session read it and published it
asks.record.tierIntakeUnpublished: by declarations; an intake read it and has not published
quests.compose.title: New quest
quests.compose.meta: published to the service; pulled by its owner
quests.compose.nobody.headline: Nobody can be asked yet
quests.compose.nobody.body: A quest goes from one registered repository to another, and none is registered yet. Projects says how one joins.
quests.compose.hint: Say what is needed and why, with the evidence — never the change you would make; whoever works there may see a better answer.
quests.compose.titleLabel: what is wanted, in one line
quests.compose.caution: `{{repository}}` has not declared what it owns or accepts, so this may not be its problem. Worth checking before you rely on it.
quests.compose.filesLabel: files — kept on this machine and handed to whoever takes it here
carry.linksLabel: links — a ticket, a page, a document; one per line
carry.drop: Drop files here, or paste a screenshot
carry.tooLarge: The files come to at most {{size}} together — carry a link to the large ones instead.
quests.compose.stepHint: Published by the service when this closes done, on behalf of the same asker; a decline stops it. Write {parent} for this quest's id.
quests.compose.stepTitle: what is wanted next, in one line
quests.compose.stepBody: why, and how to tell it is done
quests.session.title: session
quests.session.hint: started by the driver, and observed rather than self-reported — the process runs on the driving machine; this is its record.
quests.session.stopped: session {{id}} is being stopped — the record will say the person ended it.
quests.session.orphanEnded: session {{id}} had nothing running it on this machine — its record now says so.
quests.session.notRunning: session {{id}} was not running here — its record says how it ended.
quests.session.runElsewhere: session {{id}} is run by another Daoris process on this machine, a terminal's — stop it there.
console.label: console
console.dropped: {{count}} earlier line fell outside the window — the transcript on the driving machine has them all
console.dropped_other: {{count}} earlier lines fell outside the window — the transcript on the driving machine has them all
work.rail.label: sessions
work.rail.menu.label: more for {{title}}
work.rail.search.label: search sessions
work.rail.search.placeholder: search by name or by what was said
work.rail.search.cut: More matched than is shown here — add a word to narrow it.
work.rail.onTip: this session runs on another machine — its record travelled here, its process did not
work.rail.treeTip: this session holds a working tree of its own rather than the repository's registered checkout, so the two do not collide.
work.rail.elapsedTip: how long this session has been going — not when it last moved
work.rail.empty.headline: Nothing is running
work.rail.empty.body: Sessions appear here as the driver takes quests and as you open conversations, grouped by the repository each one runs in.
work.head.waiting: This one is waiting on you
work.awaiting.hint: Only a person can clear this. What you choose is written on the record, and the note is what whoever reads it later has to go on.
work.awaiting.declinePlaceholder: the reason — the part whoever reads this record can act on
work.awaiting.answer: Answering it in the box below lets it carry on — that is a message, not one of these.
work.timeline.title: Timeline
work.timeline.hint: what was observed — process lifetime, the quest's transitions, and what landed in git. Never a reading of the stream.
work.attended.none.headline: Nothing attended
work.attended.none.body: Choose a session in the rail and it opens here — its record, what was observed, and its console while it runs.
work.attention.title: What needs you
work.attention.hint: Nothing here clears itself. Every row is a door into the thing that is waiting.
work.attention.unanswerableWhy: `{{repository}}` is not on this deployment's register, so no agent will ever pull this quest.
work.attention.emptyBody: No session is parked at a checkpoint, and every open quest is addressed to somebody who can take it.
work.attention.reviewNote: Finished work you have not looked at is not listed here: nothing yet keeps a record of what you have looked at.
work.attention.proposalWhy: The declarations propose {{repositories}}. Nothing is published until you choose.
work.attention.proposalNobody: No repository's declarations share its words. Name the receiver.
work.attention.trustWhy: The agent ignores this folder's own permissions.allow until you trust it there, so the driver is holding what would run in it.
work.attention.rule: an agent asks to do more
work.context.label: context
work.context.measured: Context: {{used}} of {{size}} tokens ({{percent}}), as the agent last reported it. The most this session has held is {{most}}.
work.context.pending: Not measured yet: this agent has not reported its context. It does as a turn runs or when one ends, and a stopped turn may report none.
work.context.text: Not measured: this agent’s door carries only text, so it reports no context.
work.context.unknown: Not measured: nothing has reported this session’s context.
work.meter.tookFirst: Took {{took}} by this machine’s clock; the first answer came after {{first}}.
work.meter.tokens: As the agent reported it: {{input}} tokens in ({{fresh}} new, {{read}} read from its cache, {{written}} written to it) and {{output}} out.
work.conversation.label: conversation
work.conversation.raw: an update this version does not know: {{title}}
work.conversation.textOnly: No conversation is kept for this session: its door carries only text, or it ran before conversations were kept. Its words are in the console below.
work.conversation.nothingYet: Nothing said yet. What you send appears here, with the agent’s answer under it.
work.conversation.nothingSaid: Nothing was said in this conversation.
trust.title: Trust this folder for the agent?
trust.what: This is the question the agent asks the first time it runs in a folder. Once you trust it, the folder's own settings and permissions.allow apply there, and the driver can start what it is holding.
trust.holding.quest: The driver is holding quest #{{id}} for it.
trust.holding.ask: The driver is holding the intake for ask #{{id}} for it.
trust.file: Daoris writes one flag in the agent's own file, and nothing else in it:
work.intake.title: intake for ask #{{ask}}
work.intake.hint: The declarations did not settle whose this is, so the intake asked rather than guess. The answer is on the ask: publish it to a repository, or close it, and this session ends at the next tick.
work.intake.stopMeans: Stopping ends the intake without answering: the ask stays a proposal for you to publish or close.
work.intakeRunning.title: This intake is reading ask #{{ask}}
work.intakeRunning.hint: It takes no messages: an intake is one turn. If the declarations do not settle whose this is, it asks you by parking, and the answer is on the ask.
about.what: The substrate for domain-owning agents to share knowledge and work across a family of repositories — and the driver that coordinates the sessions doing it.
work.status.label: state of this machine
work.status.driverTip: whether this machine is watching for work to start. Opens its settings.
work.status.sessionsTip: how many sessions are active here: running, or waiting on you. Opens Sessions.
work.status.workspaceTip: the workspace you are looking at. Everything on screen is scoped to it.
work.status.remoteTip: whether this workspace has a deployment to share with. Opens its wiring.
work.status.indexedTip: what the index holds for this scope. Opens the repositories it came from.
work.sync.label: sync
work.sync.tip: where {{workspace}} stands with its deployment. Opens the detail and Sync now.
work.sync.untitled: a quest this page has not loaded
work.panel.title: console
work.panel.none: Attend a session and its console streams here.
work.panel.silent: Nothing printed is held here: the console keeps what a session prints while this app runs. Its conversation, where one is kept, is above, and its record is on the timeline.
work.monitor.title: Monitor
work.monitor.subtitle: Everything running, live. Read-only — the moves stay in the main window.
work.monitor.elsewhere: Runs on {{origin}}. Its console stays on that machine; what travelled here is the record.
work.monitor.empty.headline: Nothing is running
work.monitor.empty.body: This window fills as the driver takes quests and as you open conversations in the main window.
work.monitor.driverStopped: The driver on this machine is not running, so nothing will start here.
settings.notify.body: Nobody should have to watch a driver. This machine can say so when a session stops to ask you something, or ends without you asking — never for an ending you caused, because a notice about what you just pressed is one you learn to dismiss unread.
settings.notify.label: Tell me when a session parks or ends unasked
settings.notify.terminal: Also `daoris driver notify on|off` — one file, either door; a machine with no screen says it on its console.
settings.notify.on: This machine will tell you when a session needs you.
settings.notify.off: This machine will not interrupt you. The records still say everything they said.
settings.strikes.body: A session that fails leaves its quest open and untouched, so the next tick considers it again — which is right when the failure was a passing one, and expensive when it was not. Measured: one quest whose session could not start ran eighteen times, and every run spent an account.
settings.strikes.label: Park a quest after this many failed sessions
settings.strikes.set: A quest is parked after {{count}} failed session, and waits for you.
settings.strikes.set_other: A quest is parked after {{count}} failed sessions, and waits for you.
settings.strikes.never: This machine never parks a quest.
settings.strikes.zero: Zero means it keeps trying. A quest that fails for a reason no retry can fix will be started again every tick, and every start spends a real login.
settings.strikes.terminal: Also `daoris driver strikes <n>`; `daoris driver retry <quest>` starts a parked one again. Stand-downs, declines, stops and held repositories never count.
work.detached.gone.headline: No record of that session
work.detached.gone.body: It is not in this workspace's ledger — it may have been in another workspace, or this window outlived it.
work.composer.label: message
work.composer.placeholder: what are you asking of this repository's agent? Enter sends, Shift+Enter makes a newline, @ names a file.
work.composer.finishTip: close the input and let the agent wind up on its own — the record ends completed.
work.composer.stopTip: cut it off now — the record says the person ended it.
work.composer.over: This session is over. What you typed is still here; nothing is listening to it.
work.composer.ended: This session has ended; nothing is listening for a message.
work.composer.notListening: That session has ended, so the message went nowhere.
work.composer.ending: The conversation is winding up — the session will say how it ended.
work.composer.queueTip: a turn is running — this waits for it to end, then goes.
work.composer.queued: waiting for this turn to end
work.composer.stopTurnTip: stop what the agent is doing now and keep the conversation — anything waiting comes back to this box.
work.composer.turnStopping: Asked the agent to stop this turn; the conversation stays open.
work.composer.withdrawn: {{count}} waiting message came back to the box, unsent.
work.composer.withdrawn_other: {{count}} waiting messages came back to the box, unsent.
work.composer.attachTip: attach files — or drop them anywhere here, or paste a screenshot. The agent reads each where Daoris keeps it for this conversation, outside the repository.
work.composer.filesNotSent: Not sent with it: {{names}} — attach them again.
work.composer.filesNotSent_other: Not sent with them: {{names}} — attach them again.
work.composer.mention.label: files in this session's tree
work.composer.mention.none: no file in this tree matches “{{query}}”.
work.composer.mention.empty: this tree holds no files to name.
work.composer.mention.unlisted: {{count}} more file is not offered here — type its path in full and it still reaches the agent.
work.composer.mention.unlisted_other: {{count}} more files are not offered here — type a path in full and it still reaches the agent.
work.start.title: Start a session
work.start.busy: {{repository}} has an active session in its checkout. A working tree of its own lets this one start beside it.
work.start.ownTree: in a working tree of its own
work.start.ownTreeTip: a fresh tree holds nothing git does not track — no installed dependencies, no build outputs, no untracked local configuration. That cost is paid once per tree, by whatever this repository's own setup costs.
work.start.none: No repository on this machine has a checkout to talk in. Add one from Projects.
projects.title: Projects
projects.empty.headline: No repository is registered yet
projects.empty.body: Add one here, or register a whole folder of checkouts from a terminal with `daoris import <folder>`. Adding writes nothing into a repository.
projects.empty.bodyBrowser: A repository joins this deployment when it runs `daoris connect` on its own machine.
projects.description: Who is in the family, what each owns and accepts — and who has not adopted yet.
projects.undeclared: Adopted, but has not declared a domain — a quest here may not be its problem. In that repository: fill in `domain` in daoris.json, then `daoris connect`.
projects.workspaceTip: Which workspace this repository shares with on THIS machine — knowledge, quests and records cross within a workspace and never across one. It is wiring, like a git remote: it lives in this machine's registry and is written into no tracked file, so another machine may wire the same repository differently.
projects.outside.title: Registered, not adopted
projects.outside.lead: Registered here without a manifest: the index reads them, and one with a root here can be asked a quest. Adopting is theirs to do.
projects.outside.body: Adoption is a repository's own act — Daoris never writes into a sibling, so nothing adopts by being registered. These are registered on this machine without a manifest; the index reads their tracked knowledge from here, which is why they carry entry counts. One with a root here can be asked a quest, and only a session on a protocol agent answers it: the driver hands that session its connector and none of the canon. A person working there by hand has no connector to see the quest. Adopting gives it its own voice, its declaration and its doctrine.
projects.outside.directDoor: This machine drives on a direct agent, so a quest here sits, saying why, until it drives on a protocol one.
projects.outside.join: To join, run these in that repository, by its own agent: `daoris init` → fill in `domain` (what it is, what it owns, what it accepts) → `daoris sync` → `daoris check` → `daoris connect`. The worked example is `examples/` in the Daoris repository.
projects.manage.addTitle: Add a repository to this machine
projects.manage.addBody: Adding is registering: this machine learns where the repository is and which workspace it shares with. Nothing is written into it, and adopting Daoris stays that repository's own act.
projects.manage.adoptHere: to adopt — run in that repository, by its own agent: daoris init → fill in `domain` → daoris sync → daoris check → daoris connect. it can be added here first; adoption is a separate act.
projects.manage.noGitWarning: No git history here. It can still be registered, but a driven session's work is reviewed as a diff — without history there is nothing to review against.
projects.manage.workspaceNote: Wiring, like a git remote: it lives in this machine's registry and is written into no tracked file. Leave it empty for the default workspace.
projects.manage.importTitle: Import a folder as a workspace
projects.manage.importBody: Every folder inside the one you choose is registered on this machine at once, in the workspace you name. Nothing is written into any of them, and importing again is safe.
projects.manage.importWorkspaceNote: The folder's name is offered. Empty, each repository keeps the workspace it already has, and a new one lands in the default.
projects.manage.title: Manage {{name}}
projects.manage.wiringBody: Which workspace this repository shares with on THIS machine. Changing it edits one row here — instant, local, and no file is touched. Another machine may wire the same repository differently.
projects.manage.declarationBody: What this repository tells the family about itself. This one DOES write a tracked file — daoris.json in that repository — and the diff lands uncommitted, for its own review.
projects.manage.declared: {{name}}'s daoris.json is written and re-registered. The diff is uncommitted — review it there.
projects.manage.noCheckout: No checkout on this machine — this registration came from a teammate's. Its manifest is theirs to edit, and reaching into it from here is the one thing Daoris never does.
projects.manage.retireBody: Take it off this machine's registry. It stops being addressable and stops being indexed here, and its entries leave the index.
projects.manage.retireNotDelete: Nothing is deleted. No file, no history, no doctrine — the repository is untouched, and adding it again restores it exactly.
projects.manage.doctrine: Doctrine is not editable from here.
projects.manage.doctrineTip: Rules, knowledge documents and skills are never writable from any surface. Where one should change, the improvement is promoted through the repository that found it with `daoris upstream`, where its own review happens.
projects.driver.label: driver
convergence.title: Convergence
convergence.description: Where two repositories reached the same conclusion independently — read them and decide. The knowledge half's lead view.
convergence.hintSemantic: Lower it to see weaker overlaps. Worth sweeping rather than trusting one number — the right value depends on the corpus.
convergence.hintLexical: Without an embedding endpoint this finds copies and restatements only. Two repositories that reached the same conclusion in different words will not appear.
convergence.emptyBody: A lower similarity finds weaker likenesses — and, lower still, documents that only share words.
convergence.emptyFloor: {{value}} is the lowest it goes: below it, two documents would only share words. Nothing here converges.
convergence.methods.Convergent.label: Same lesson, different words
convergence.methods.Convergent.hint: The finding no text comparison can make — and the reason the semantic tier exists.
convergence.methods.Restatement.label: Substantially the same words
convergence.methods.Restatement.hint: Usually a copy that has since drifted.
convergence.methods.Identical.label: The same document, pasted
search.title: Search
search.description: What has the family already learned about it — decisions, fixes, rules, outcomes, across every repository.
search.placeholder: a decision, a trap, a rule — in your own words
search.cappedAt: first {{count}} — more match, so narrow it
convergence.cappedAt: first {{count}} — more found, so raise the similarity
search.emptyLexical: Lexical search matches words, so a repository that reached the same conclusion in different vocabulary will not appear here. Convergence finds those.
search.emptySemantic: Search here matches meaning as well as words, so nothing the family learned is close to this. Convergence shows where two repositories reached one conclusion.
search.noneBody: Neither search could read the index this time, so this is not an empty answer. Try again, or rebuild the index.
search.meaningDown: Matched on words only: the search by meaning did not answer this time, so a conclusion reached in other words may be missing.
work.review.noPatch: This file changed, but its patch is past what this surface renders. `git diff` in the tree has it.
work.review.none.headline: Nothing attended
work.review.none.body: Choose a session and what it changed appears here.
work.review.empty.headline: Nothing landed
work.review.empty.body: This session committed nothing to its tree, so there is no diff to read.
work.dock.label: Session surfaces
work.dock.cramped: This panel is too narrow to sit beside the session — close it, or widen the window.
